I guess this has been going on for… maybe a year? Hard to say exactly. Since I’ve been retired it’s become more noticeable. My wife points it out a lot. She’ll ask me to take the bins out, or ring the electrician, and I’ll say “yes, yes,” but then I get distracted and it just doesn’t get done. It’s not that I’m refusing, it just sort of slips away from me, and then she’s annoyed that I’ve “ignored” her.

I keep misplacing things I need. My glasses, the TV remote, letters that I’ve put “somewhere safe.” I’ll put the car keys down and five minutes later I’m wandering around the house muttering to myself. It makes me feel a bit on edge, like I’m not on top of things.

I also forget everyday stuff more than I used to—returning calls, paying a bill I meant to sort out, or we’ll have an appointment and I’ll mix up the time unless my wife reminds me. Then I start worrying I’m letting people down or that there’s something wrong with me, and that worry itself can make it harder to focus, if that makes sense.

I’d say it’s been maybe the last six months or so that this has really started bothering me. On site, my foreman will tell me how he wants something framed, I nod along, think I got it, then halfway through I realize I missed a step or mixed up what order he wanted things in. It’s not like I don’t care—I just sort of drift, and then I’m playing catch-up.

My tools go missing all the time. I’ll set my tape or drill down “just for a second” and then waste ten minutes walking around trying to remember where I left it. Same thing at home—misplacing my keys, my wallet, even my phone when it’s in my pocket sometimes.

My wife’s getting frustrated because I keep forgetting basic stuff—she’ll ask me to grab milk on the way home or call the plumber, and it just slips my mind. I’ve missed a couple of dentist appointments because I didn’t put them in my phone or I saw the reminder and then got distracted.

Lately I’ve been more on edge about it, kind of worrying I’m screwing up at work or letting my family down, which probably makes it even harder to focus.
